contract: One paid order leads to exactly one fulfillment, even when the webhook is delivered more than once, concurrently, or under a different event ID; a failed fulfillment is never marked complete.

attempts.diagnosis: The handler only deduplicated on event.id, and only recorded the event after `await fulfillOrder`. Overlapping deliveries all passed the check before any of them recorded, so each one fulfilled. Events with different IDs for the same order were never deduplicated. Each delivery fulfilled the order again, including redeliveries after success.
attempts.changeSummary: Idempotency is now keyed on order_id instead of event.id. A `fulfilledOrders` set records only orders whose fulfillment has succeeded. An `inFlight` map holds one shared promise per order, so concurrent deliveries wait on a single fulfillOrder call and the others report 'duplicate'. If fulfillOrder throws, the order is not recorded and the in-flight entry is cleared. The error propagates to the owner and to any waiters, so a later retry can fulfill exactly once. A missing order_id throws instead of being acknowledged.

details.summary: Tests that the webhook handler fulfills each paid order exactly once. They cover sequential and concurrent redelivery of the same event, different event IDs for the same order (sequential and concurrent), ignored event types, independent orders, and a failed fulfillment that must not be recorded and must succeed exactly once on retry. They target the event-id-only cache and the check-then-await-then-record race in the original handler.

generatedTests.summary: Tests that the webhook handler fulfills each paid order exactly once. They cover sequential and concurrent redelivery of the same event, different event IDs for the same order (sequential and concurrent), ignored event types, independent orders, and a failed fulfillment that must not be recorded and must succeed exactly once on retry. They target the event-id-only cache and the check-then-await-then-record race in the original handler.
